note: base + contributor inputs -> expected merged catalog. `expect_diagnostics` is hand-asserted; `expected` and `expected_sha256` are generated and must be reproduced byte-identically by Jawaka's compiler.

cases.name: accept-new-system
cases.note: the ordinary case: a new system id, no namespace collision.

cases.name: accept-system-extension
cases.note: system_extensions[] is the ONLY way to touch an existing system; the alternate core is appended, nothing is restated.

cases.name: accept-frontend-core
cases.note: a retroarch core that ships its own RetroArch frontend (LEAF-RA-1), added to an existing system. The merge copies an accepted core entry through verbatim, so `frontend` reaches the merged core row unchanged and still pak-relative, beside the generated provider and status.

cases.name: base-collision-system-id
cases.note: a systems[] entry whose id already exists is a COLLISION, not an override. Overriding a first-party system is a non-goal.

diagnostics.detail: system SNES claims system_id=snes already owned by the release catalog

cases.name: base-collision-pattern
cases.note: P1-5: a unique id is not enough. Folder matching is first-match-wins, so claiming another system's pattern steals its ROM folder.

diagnostics.detail: system SCUMMVM claims pattern=snes already owned by the release catalog
system SCUMMVM claims rom_root=roms/snes already owned by the release catalog

cases.name: base-collision-image-root
cases.note: the system is refused for its image_root claim alone. Its core is untouched and stays in the catalog -- refusing a system does not retract a core another pak may extend a system with.

diagnostics.detail: system SCUMMVM claims image_root=images/snes already owned by the release catalog

cases.name: base-collision-core-id
cases.note: the core collides and is dropped; the system survives because default_core snes9x still resolves -- to the RELEASE core, which is exactly what should happen.

diagnostics.detail: core snes9x claims core_id=snes9x already owned by the release catalog

cases.name: base-collision-config-folder
cases.note: case-folded: 'snes9x' collides with the release 'Snes9x'. RetroArch would otherwise write both cores' saves into one FAT32 directory.

diagnostics.detail: core scummvm claims config_folder=snes9x already owned by the release catalog
system SCUMMVM needs core scummvm, which is not available after merge; the system is refused too rather than producing a tile that cannot launch

cases.name: base-collision-info-name
cases.note: materialized .info FILENAMES share one merged directory, so the basename is a namespace even though the pak-relative paths differ.

diagnostics.detail: core scummvm claims info_name=snes9x_libretro.info already owned by the release catalog
system SCUMMVM needs core scummvm, which is not available after merge; the system is refused too rather than producing a tile that cannot launch

cases.name: contributor-collision-both-refused
cases.note: D9: BOTH sides are refused. Never resolved by readdir order -- a contract that depends on directory iteration is not a contract.

diagnostics.detail: system ALPHA claims rom_root=roms/scummvm, also claimed by mlp1/Beta.pak; both refused
system BETA claims rom_root=roms/scummvm, also claimed by mlp1/Alpha.pak; both refused

cases.name: casefold-contributor-collision
cases.note: matching is already case-insensitive, so 'SCUMMVM' and 'scummvm' are the same claim.

diagnostics.detail: system ALPHA claims pattern=scummvm, also claimed by mlp1/Beta.pak; both refused
system BETA claims pattern=scummvm, also claimed by mlp1/Alpha.pak; both refused

cases.name: default-core-unavailable
cases.note: the pak's core is refused for a base collision, so its system is refused too. A tile that cannot launch is worse than no tile -- dependency cleanup is part of the merge.

diagnostics.detail: core scummvm claims config_folder=snes9x already owned by the release catalog
system SCUMMVM needs core scummvm, which is not available after merge; the system is refused too rather than producing a tile that cannot launch

cases.name: unknown-default-core
cases.note: distinct from default-core-unavailable: nothing was refused, the manifest simply names a core that exists nowhere. Different diagnosis, different developer fix.

diagnostics.detail: system SCUMMVM needs core nosuchcore, which is not available after merge; the system is refused too rather than producing a tile that cannot launch

cases.name: dangling-extension-system
cases.note: T-5: an extension whose system is absent after merge is dropped and logged, not silently ignored.

diagnostics.detail: system_extensions names NOSUCH, which no system provides after merge; extension dropped

cases.name: dangling-alternate-core
cases.note: the extension is ACCEPTED and the one bad name dropped: a single typo should not cost the developer the other entries.

diagnostics.detail: system_extensions for SNES names core ghost, absent after merge; that name dropped, extension accepted

cases.name: refusal-cascade
cases.note: one pass is not enough. Alpha's core collides with the base, which refuses Alpha's system, which strands Beta's extension on that system. Cleanup iterates to a fixed point.

diagnostics.detail: core alpha claims config_folder=snes9x already owned by the release catalog
system ALPHA needs core alpha, which is not available after merge; the system is refused too rather than producing a tile that cannot launch
system_extensions names ALPHA, which no system provides after merge; extension dropped
